idiom_name: List<data class> mapped from Exposed ResultRow / JDBC ResultSet
implementation_notes: Kotlin's record set is a List of immutable data classes: with Exposed you query inside transaction { } and map each ResultRow - a typed accessor over the JDBC ResultSet - into a data class (Users.select(Users.id, Users.email).map { UserDto(it[Users.id], it[Users.email]) }); plain JDBC is the same story with ResultSet.getX plus a manual mapping loop, and JPA returns List<Entity> directly. What replaces the classic row/column container is the data class plus the collection, with the column header consumed once at the mapping site. The generic tabular form survives only for dynamic exports, where ResultRow (a FieldSet addressable by column object or index) is the library equivalent of a record set.
pitfalls: ResultRow is bound to its transaction: storing it and mapping after transaction { } returns throws at access time - materialise the data classes inside the block.
NULL columns need nullable properties (Long?); a non-null field throws on the first NULL row, and Kotlin only helps if the mapping spells the nullability.
Mapping is O(rows) allocations: for large exports stream with a Sequence (or LIMIT/page) instead of building one big List.
